title: How to Interrupt Politely
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：会议控场

sections.heading: 1. Interrupting Is a Service
paragraphs: Many of us were taught that interrupting is rude.
So when a colleague spends ten minutes on a side topic, we sit and wait, and the real agenda gets ==squeezed== into the last five minutes.
Everyone leaves annoyed, including the person who was talking.
Think about who pays for that politeness.
Eight people lose ten minutes each, and the decision you needed gets __pushed to next week__.
**Letting a meeting drift is not polite; it just spreads the cost around.**
A good interruption is ==brief==, warm, and useful.
It protects the group's time without ==embarrassing== the speaker.
The trick is to __cut in__ on the topic, not on the person.
paragraphs_zh: 我们很多人从小被教育，打断别人是不礼貌的。
所以同事在一个跑题的话题上讲了十分钟，我们就坐着等，真正的议程被挤到最后五分钟。
最后每个人都一肚子火，包括刚才那个讲话的人。
想想这份客气是谁在买单。
八个人每人损失十分钟，本该做的决定又被推到了下周。
放任会议跑偏并不是礼貌，只是把代价摊给了所有人。
好的打断要简短、友善、有用。
它既保护了大家的时间，又不会让讲话的人难堪。
诀窍是打断话题，而不是打断人。

sections.heading: 2. The Name, Thanks, Bridge Pattern
paragraphs: Start with the person's name.
Hearing their name makes people pause ==naturally==, so you don't have to raise your voice.
"Priya, sorry to jump in here."
Then give them credit for the point.
"That's a really good question about the logging format."
This ==signals== that you are not dismissing them, only __changing the timing__.
Finally, build a bridge back to the agenda.
"Can we __park it__ for the end, so we can finish the rollout plan first?"
**Always offer the topic a home, a later slot, a separate thread, or a follow-up call.**
People let go much more easily when they know their idea will not just disappear.
On video calls, timing is harder, because a small delay makes everyone talk over each other.
Use the raise hand button or a short message in the chat first, then speak when there is a gap.
If you ==chair== the meeting, say at the start that you will keep things on track, so nobody takes it personally later.
paragraphs_zh: 先叫对方的名字。
人听到自己的名字会自然停下来，你不用提高嗓门。
「Priya，不好意思插一句。」
然后肯定一下对方的观点。
「关于日志格式，这个问题提得很好。」
这是在表明你没有否定他，只是换个时间讨论。
最后，搭一座桥回到议程上。
「这个我们能不能放到最后聊，先把上线方案过完？」
一定要给这个话题安排个去处，比如后面的时间、单独拉个群，或者另约个会。
大家知道自己的想法不会就这么没了，放手就容易得多。
开视频会时时机更难把握，因为稍有延迟大家就会抢话。
先用举手按钮或者在聊天框里发条短消息，等有空当了再开口。
如果你是主持人，开场就说清楚你会把控节奏，这样之后没人会往心里去。

gist.q: 作者为什么说放任跑题并不礼貌？
gist.a: 每个人都在为这份“礼貌”买单：八个人各浪费十分钟，该做的决定被推到下周，只是把成本分摊开了。

gist.q: 礼貌打断的三步模式是什么？
gist.a: 先叫对方名字让他自然停下；肯定他的观点；再搭桥回到议程，比如把话题挪到会后。

gist.q: 为什么要给被打断的话题“安排一个去处”？
gist.a: 对方知道自己的想法不会就此消失，才更容易放手。

prompts.q: 上线评审会上，一位同事开始详细讲他对日志格式的意见，已经说了五分钟，离会议结束只剩十五分钟。用 30 秒礼貌打断他，并给这个话题安排去处。
prompts.ref: Arjun, sorry to jump in. That's a fair point about the log format, and I think it deserves a proper discussion. We only have fifteen minutes left, though, and we still need a go or no-go on the release. Could we park the logging question and pick it up in a separate thread this afternoon? I'll start the thread myself right after this call.
prompts.ref_zh: Arjun，不好意思插一句。你说的日志格式确实有道理，也值得好好讨论。不过我们只剩十五分钟了，还得定这次发布上不上。日志的问题能不能先放一放，下午单独拉个群聊？会一结束我就去拉群。

prompts.q: 线上会议，你作为主持人在开场时先打个招呼：今天议程紧，你可能会打断大家。用 30 秒说得友好又不让人尴尬。
prompts.ref: Before we start, a quick heads-up. We have three big items today and only forty-five minutes. So if a topic starts to run long, I might jump in and suggest we move it to the end or to a follow-up. Please don't take it personally, it's just to protect everyone's time. And feel free to do the same to me if I start rambling.
prompts.ref_zh: 开始之前先提个醒。我们今天有三个大议题，只有四十五分钟。所以如果某个话题聊得太久，我可能会插一句，建议挪到最后或者会后再跟进。大家别往心里去，只是为了保护每个人的时间。如果我自己讲着讲着跑题了，你们也尽管打断我。

words.ex: We squeezed the security review into the last day of the sprint.
Keep the status update brief, two minutes per team.
I didn't want to embarrass him by pointing out the bug in front of the client.
Once the tests were green, the conversation naturally moved to the launch date.
Moving the deadline signals that quality matters more than speed.
Who's chairing the incident review tomorrow?
Let's park the pricing question until we have data.
Sorry to cut in, but the build just failed again.
Don't dismiss that alert; it fired before the last outage too.
